headline: Democrats take Congress: oil sinks 8% on peace hopes, gold back above $4,000, Treasuries rally
summary: The Democratic sweep of both chambers was read as a check on the Iran war, so WTI fell 8.3% to $88.12 and RBOB 7.1% to $2.73, ignoring bullish EIA draws. A weaker dollar and a 4–7bp Treasury rally, with the 10-year near 4.89%, lifted gold 3.4% back above $4,000 and silver 5.1%. Bunds lagged on a 4.0% euro-area inflation print, while OATs rallied about 5bp as spreads tightened.
drivers: Midterm sweep drains oil's war premium

Democrats won the House and Senate and plan a War Powers vote on further action around Hormuz, while Trump said he had no immediate plans to strike Iran. WTI settled -$7.97 at $88.12 and Brent -$8.98 at $94.62, WTI's lowest since Aug 31, despite a fifth straight EIA crude draw.
Gridlock and softer data rally Treasuries

The 2-year fell about 6bp to near 4.55% and the 10-year about 6bp to 4.89%, a two-month low, as divided government limits new spending and the refunding kept auction sizes unchanged. ISM services slipped to 54.5 vs 54.8 expected, though December hike odds held near 80%.

Comex gold settled +$133.20 (+3.4%) at $4,061.10, its biggest gain since early August, as the dollar hit a one-month low and real yields fell. Silver jumped 5.1% to $52.12, narrowing the gold/silver ratio to about 78.
Euro inflation holds Bunds back; OATs tighten

Euro-area inflation rose to 4.0% in October and Nagel called a December ECB hike very likely necessary, so the Bund 10-year held near 3.32% and the 2-year rose about 2bp. OATs fell about 5bp to 4.88%, tightening the spread to near 157bp; the Assembly rejected the budget's revenue part late in the day as expected.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled -$7.97 (-8.3%) at $88.12, the lowest since Aug 31; Jan Brent -$8.98 at $94.62, back under $100.
oil.why: Democrats took both the House and Senate, and traders read that as a brake on the Iran war: Democratic leaders plan a War Powers vote to force approval for any further action around Hormuz, and Trump said he has no immediate plans to strike Iran. With Gulf exports already recovering, the war premium collapsed, swamping a fifth straight EIA crude draw (-0.9 million barrels vs a forecast build). WTI is down $16, or 15%, in three sessions.
oil.outlook: Bias lower in an $84–94 range as the risk premium keeps leaking, with $87 the first support and the late-August lows in the low $80s below that. A breakdown in the Qatar-brokered US–Iran talks or a new Hormuz incident would quickly put $94–96 back in play.
oil.watch: US–Iran MOU headlines, the War Powers push, EIA stocks Nov 12 and Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11.

gas.note: Dec RBOB fell 20.69¢ (-7.1%) to $2.7286, the lowest settle since March 10; AAA pump average $4.12, down 12¢ in a week.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude lower as the midterm result drained the war premium from the whole barrel, with ULSD down a similar 7.2% to $4.2055. EIA data were bullish on paper, with gasoline stocks down 0.2 million barrels and distillates down 3.6 million to their lowest since 2003, but traders ignored them. The cheaper winter blend and fading demand keep pulling the pump average toward $4.
gas.outlook: Range $2.60–2.90 with a downside bias while crude slides; tight distillate stocks should limit RBOB's discount to diesel cracks rather than lift gasoline. A rebound in crude above $94 or an unplanned Gulf Coast refinery outage would put $2.90 back in reach.
gas.watch: Crude and Iran headlines, EIA stocks Nov 12 and refinery restarts after maintenance.

gold.note: Comex Nov settled +$133.20 (+3.4%) at $4,061.10, its biggest gain since Aug 5; spot ended near $4,060, back above $4,000.
gold.why: The Democratic sweep knocked the dollar to a one-month low and pulled Treasury yields down 4–7bp, with the 10-year near 4.89%, a two-month low, cutting the cost of holding bullion. Analysts also cited fiscal and policy uncertainty from a divided government and demand for protection against a more confrontational White House. A softer ISM services print (54.5 vs 54.8 expected) helped, even though December hike odds stayed near 80%.
gold.outlook: Bias higher in a $3,950–4,150 range now that $4,000 has been reclaimed, with $4,100 the next resistance. A hot payrolls report Nov 6 that lifts real yields and the dollar could push it back below $4,000.
gold.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, Fed speakers and US CPI next week.

silver.note: Comex Nov settled +$2.53 (+5.1%) at $52.12, its best day since June 12; spot near $52.30.
silver.why: Silver outran gold as the falling dollar and yields triggered short covering after last week's slide to a 2026 low of $49.10 settle on Oct 30. Its higher beta to risk appetite also helped as stocks rallied on the election result. The gold/silver ratio narrowed to about 78 from 79, a sign that some of the forced liquidation is fading.
silver.outlook: Range $50–55 with a recovering bias while gold holds above $4,000. A close back under $50 would reopen the lows near $49; a move above $54 would point to a broader rebound.
silver.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, China trade and inflation data and the dollar.

us2y.note: Down about 6bp to near 4.55%, a two-month low, after the Democratic sweep; December hike odds near 80%.
us2y.why: The front end rallied overnight as the results came in and the dollar slid, then extended gains when ISM services slipped to 54.5 against 54.8 expected, with prices paid easing to 73.0 instead of rising. ADP's 86,000 October jobs beat forecasts but didn't change the picture. Hike pricing for December stayed around 80%, so the move was more risk repricing than a shift in Fed bets.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.48–4.65%. A soft payrolls Nov 6 would push toward 4.48%; a strong report near 100,000 with firm wages would send it back to 4.65%.
us2y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, Fed speakers and CPI next week.

us5y.note: Down about 7bp to near 4.69%, leading the rally as the belly outperformed.
us5y.why: The 5-year led the gains, falling as much as 8bp, as markets priced a divided government that blocks new fiscal expansion while the Fed is near the end of its hiking cycle. The quarterly refunding kept coupon auction sizes unchanged, easing supply fears. A slightly softer ISM services report and a drop in oil to $88 also trimmed inflation expectations.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.60–4.80% with a mild rally bias while oil slides. A strong jobs report or a rebound in crude above $95 would push it back toward 4.80%.
us5y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, CPI next week and the 3-year, 10-year and 30-year auctions.

us10y.note: Down about 6bp to near 4.89%, the lowest since early September; 2s10s held near 34bp.
us10y.why: Treasuries rallied on Democratic control of both chambers, which investors read as gridlock that limits new spending and borrowing. The refunding kept auction sizes steady, oil's 8% drop cut inflation risk, and ISM services and its prices index both came in softer than forecast. Strategists noted that blocking new spending does not shrink the existing deficit, which limited the rally.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.80–5.00% with a mild rally bias while oil keeps falling. A hot payrolls or CPI print, or a sloppy 10-year auction, would put 5% back in play; 4.80% is the next support.
us10y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, the 10-year auction and CPI next week.

us30y.note: Down about 4bp to near 5.28%, lagging the belly as the curve steadied.
us30y.why: The long bond rallied with the curve as gridlock lowered the risk of fresh fiscal stimulus and the refunding left auction sizes unchanged, easing term premium worries. It lagged the 5-year because divided government does not cut the existing deficit and inflation is still running well above target, with ISM services prices at 73.0. Lower oil gave some relief on breakevens.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.40%. A clean 30-year auction next week and calmer oil would let it test 5.20%; a weak auction or hot CPI would push it back above 5.35%.
us30y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, the 30-year auction and CPI next week.

de2y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.05% as euro-area inflation hit a three-year high of 4.0%.
de2y.why: October flash inflation rose to 4.0% from 3.8%, while core held at 2.5%, and Bundesbank President Nagel said a December rate hike is very likely necessary. That kept the front end under pressure even as Treasuries rallied, with markets pricing about an 80% chance of a December ECB hike. The euro-area front end ignored most of the US election rally.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.98–3.12% with a mild upward bias as ECB hike pricing firms. A softer run of euro-area data or a big drop in oil could take it back toward 3.00%.
de2y.watch: ECB speakers, euro-area PMIs and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.14%, little changed as hot inflation offset the Treasury rally.
de5y.why: The belly was pulled two ways: the 4.0% euro-area inflation print and hawkish ECB talk lifted front-end yields, while the US rally and oil's slide toward $88 helped longer bonds. The net was a near-flat day after Monday's multi-week low. Oil's fall softens the energy-driven inflation path that has pushed the ECB toward hikes.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.05–3.20%. Holding below 3.20% while oil falls keeps the bias neutral; a renewed oil spike or hawkish ECB guidance would push it higher.
de5y.watch: ECB speakers, German industrial data and euro-area PMIs.

de10y.note: Little changed near 3.32%, up less than 1bp, as hot euro inflation offset the Treasury rally.
de10y.why: Bunds lagged Treasuries because the euro-area inflation print of 4.0%, a three-year high, kept the ECB on track to hike in December. Lower oil and the drop in US yields stopped Bund yields rising further. The 10-year is still close to Monday's two-month low near 3.29%, and the curve flattened slightly.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.25–3.40%. Falling oil supports a gentle rally; a break above 3.40% would need firmer ECB hike pricing or a rebound in energy prices.
de10y.watch: ECB speakers, euro-area PMIs and Bund auctions next week.

de30y.note: Down about 1bp to near 3.69%, outperforming the front end as the curve flattened.
de30y.why: The long end gained slightly as the US long-end rally and oil's 8% drop eased term premium and inflation worries, while the front end sold off on hot euro-area inflation. That flattened the Bund 2s30s curve by about 3bp. Supply and fiscal concerns remain limited for Germany compared with France.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.78%, with further flattening likely if the ECB keeps signalling a December hike. A broader global long-end selloff would test 3.78%.
de30y.watch: ECB speakers, US long-end auctions and German supply.

fr2y.note: Little changed near 3.63%, holding as hot euro inflation offset broader spread tightening.
fr2y.why: The French front end tracked the euro rates curve, held up by the 4.0% inflation print and ECB hike talk, while the broad tightening in sovereign spreads on lower oil limited the rise. The National Assembly's rejection of the budget's revenue section came late in the evening and had been widely expected. Short OATs are more sensitive to ECB pricing than to French politics.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.55–3.70%, moving with ECB expectations. A firm ECB signal for more than one hike would push it toward 3.70%.
fr2y.watch: ECB speakers, the Senate budget debate from Nov 20 and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Down about 3bp to near 4.28%, outperforming Bunds as spreads tightened.
fr5y.why: OATs beat Bunds as lower oil and the US rally tightened euro sovereign spreads broadly, with French and Italian debt both gaining. Investors had already priced the budget's first-reading defeat, and the government's plan to send its original 5% deficit text to the Senate kept the fiscal path from worsening. Fitch's recent negative outlook is largely reflected in BBB-like spreads.
fr5y.outlook: Range 4.20–4.35% with a mild tightening bias while oil falls. Talk of a 49.3 confidence vote or a government crisis would widen spreads again.
fr5y.watch: Senate budget debate from Nov 20 and any rating actions.

fr10y.note: Down about 5bp to near 4.88%; the spread to Bunds tightened about 5bp to near 157bp.
fr10y.why: OATs rallied as oil's slide and calmer geopolitics drove a broad tightening of euro sovereign spreads, with the OAT-Bund spread narrowing to about 157bp, still near this year's highs. The Assembly unanimously rejected the revenue part of the 2027 budget late in the day, a result everyone expected, sending the government's original text to the Senate. Fitch's negative outlook earlier in the week has had little lasting effect.
fr10y.outlook: Bias for the spread to drift lower toward 150bp while oil falls, with the 10-year in a 4.80–4.95% range. A 49.3 vote that risks a censure motion, or a rating downgrade, would push the spread back above 165bp.
fr10y.watch: Senate budget debate from Nov 20, 49.3 decisions and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: Down about 4bp to near 5.43%, still close to its highs.
fr30y.why: The long end joined the spread rally as lower oil and the US long-end rally eased term premium. Gains were smaller than at the 10-year because French long-dated supply and fiscal risk keep investors demanding a large premium, and the budget's rejection in the Assembly keeps the deficit path uncertain. The 30-year remains near its peak levels of the year.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.55%. A credible budget compromise could pull it toward 5.35%; fresh political turmoil or a rating downgrade would push it to new highs above 5.55%.
fr30y.watch: Senate budget debate from Nov 20, OAT auctions and rating reviews.

watch: Next: the BoE decision Nov 5, US payrolls Nov 6, Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11, US CPI and the refunding auctions next week, the French Senate budget debate from Nov 20 and the ECB Dec 17.
